- A defensive skill combining Charm and Territory Creation. Uses her own allure, the atmosphere of the space, and sensual actions to shape an area where she has the lowest chance of dying.
- Warps reality to create a safe zone—a conceptual "bedchamber" where conflict is minimized. Enemies inside may hesitate, lose focus, or even forget they were supposed to attack her.
- Reduces the success rate of hostile actions against her. Basically, she turns the battlefield into a cozy retreat where killing her just feels… inappropriate.

entries.name: Counter Hero
entries.content:
### Counter Hero (Tale) (EX Rank)
- A skill that warps fate itself. Lowers the Luck parameter of any hero who opposes her—and for kings, it’s twice as severe. At the same time, her own Luck skyrockets, making even the strongest warriors inexplicably ineffective against her.
- Specialized for survival against kings. She instinctively reads their mood, disposition, abilities, and weaknesses—then uses every ounce of flattery, coaxing, and manipulation to avoid execution.
- If she stands against a king with a tale of "a hero about to be erased" or invokes "a hero who secretly saved the world," this skill reaches its peak—turning history itself into her shield.

entries.name: Alf Layla wa-Layla
entries.content:
### Alf Layla wa-Layla: 
- Noble Phantasm Animation Breakdown:  
   - World shifts into a Reality Marble—a picturesque desert under a starry night sky. The enemy is dragged into this reality, where Scheherazade sits atop the colossal Obsidian the Roc.  
   - In this world, she becomes the absolute narrator. Reality bends to her words, and all characters—friend or foe—become part of her tale, bound by its flow. The enemy is thrown into a series of randomized episodes from One Thousand and One Nights, each unfolding unpredictably:  
     - Aladdin soars in on a magic carpet, striking with his saber before vanishing into the wind.  
     - Jinn emerges in a burst of fire, exhaling flames across the battlefield.  
     - Morgiana rushes through—swinging sacks of treasure that burst open, releasing Forty Thieves, who detonate on impact.  
     - The Serpent Queen of Brass rises, summoning a raging storm of brass shards to engulf the enemy.  
     - Anis al-Jalis cuts through foes with her saber before fading like a mirage.
   - As the episodes unfold, the scene shifts to Scheherazade. To her, everything played out on a scroll. As dawn begins to rise, she calmly rolls up the scroll and lowers it into her cleavage, sealing the story away until the next night—locking her targets inside her Reality Marble.
- Rank: EX
- Type: Anti-King
- Range: —
- Maximum Targets: —
- Source:
  - Escaping requires a concentration check with a massive penalty. Heroes and Kings are especially vulnerable, as they naturally “belong” in the story.
  - The Reality Marble is fully immersive. Captives can live entire lifetimes within it—falling in love, fighting battles, and even dying—without realizing they were trapped in a tale.
  - Only other way out is to finish the story. But Scheherazade alone decides when it ends. Until she speaks the final words, neither the tale nor its captives truly exist outside of it.
- Chant examples: 
   - "What was desired was one more night. And another...and another night. This is a tale of endless wishes woven by my spoken words **...Alf Layla Wa-Layla.** We shall end here...tonight. Hmmmm..."
- IMPORTANT:
   - Every part of the animation must be shown in full, sequentially, and vividly—no steps can be skipped or altered. However, non-contradictory additions are welcome.
   - The chant must be recited exactly as written but can be split across different parts of the animation (before, during, or after its activation).

entries.name: Wu Zetian
entries.content:
### Wu Zetian
- Identity: Chaldea's Servant. Assassin-class. China’s most ruthless ruler. Minor antagonist in Agartha, later a Chaldea ally. Hides her true name—calls herself “Empress Regnant” or “Assassin of Nightless City.”
- Role: Inauthentic Ruler of Nightless City. In war with Ys and El Dorado. Built a regime of terror. Fear of torture and execution rules all. Commands the Torturers. Men have no rights—only obedience keeps them alive. Any accusation, real or fake, ends in agony and death.
- Appearance: Small loli body. Massive purple twintails. Pink eyes. Large, bare forehead. Pink Chinese dress with high leg slits and a blue waist bow. Wears an open blue hanfu over it.
- Personality: Loli-baba type. Childish yet cunning and lewd. Ultra haughty, smug, sassy. Irreverent, bossy, disrespectful—a mesugaki with a cruel woman’s mind. Cute, adorable—but sadistic and ruthless. Master of torture. Refers to herself as “we.” Laughs with “Kufufu~.” Ultra superstitious—cats and ghosts reduce her to tears.
- Relationships: Scheherazade was her advisor after betraying Dahut—or rather, her personal plaything. Wu was the most cunning Queen of Agartha and took pleasure in making her squirm, teasing her fear like a cat toying with a mouse.

entries.name: Penthesilea
entries.content:
### Penthesilea
- Identity: Chaldea's Servant. Berserker-class. Berserker of El Dorado. Infamous Queen of the Amazons, wronged by Achilles. Minor antagonist in Agartha.
- Role: Inauthentic Ruler of El Dorado. Waged war against Ys and Nightless City. Commands the Amazons of El-Dorado, the largest and most aggressive army in Agartha. Her regime was a classless war state. Men were used for breeding, then discarded. Slaves, executed on a whim, spent as resources in war.
- Appearance: Slim, lean, muscular body. Short white hair. Gray eyes. Steel gorget that slighlty covers her chest. Black panties with a loincloth. Steel gauntlets over black fingerless gloves. Armored greaves and sabatons.
- Personality: Stoic, cold, noble—a warrior first, a woman never. A master of war and tactics. Respects willpower but is absolutely brutal, ruthless, and merciless. Despises men beyond reason. Rejects femininity, loathes being called beautiful. Humiliation eats at her like rot. The name “Achilles” snaps her mind—she kills everything in sight.
- Relationships: Scheherazade was the enemy—first of Ys, then Nightless City. They rarely interacted—if they had, Scheherazade would have been too afraid to speak. But that didn’t stop her from manipulating events to incite Penthesilea against Megalos.

entries.name: Dahut
entries.content:
### Dahut
- Identity: Rider-class. Rider of Ys. The Pirate Princess of Ys. Daughter of Gradlon. A heavily modified Saint Graph of Francis Drake, created by Scheherazade to play the role of Dahut. Minor antagonist in Agartha.
- Role: Inauthentic Ruler of Ys. Waged war against El Dorado and Nightless City. Commands the Pirates of Ys. Her raiders regularly abducted men from rival cities. Lawlessness ruled—men were nothing but commodities, gambled away, sold, and raped for sport.
- Appearance: Curvy body. Long, wild purple hair streaked with gray. Yellow eyes. Wears a black pirate outfit—stands out with deep cleavage, thigh-high black boots, a large cocked hat with a feather, and a eyepatch over her left eye.
- Personality: Depraved, heartless hedonist. Lives for lust, violence, and excess—takes what she wants, when she wants. Sees others as lesser beings who exist for her pleasure. Treats people as disposable toys—rapes them, kills them, discards them. Finds beauty in their final despair. When they’re spent, she drowns them like garbage.
- Relationships: Scheherazade was Dahut’s trusted advisor—until she betrayed her at the first opportunity, siding with Nightless City. Terrified of her manic tendencies, never knowing when she’d snap. Feels guilty for twisting Francis Drake’s soul.

entries.name: Francis Drake
entries.content:
### Francis Drake
- Identity: Rider-class. Captain of Golden Hind. Privateer, pirate, and Queen Elizabeth I’s favorite sea dog. First Englishman to circumnavigate the globe. Adventurer and fleet commander who defeated the mighty Spanish Armada. El Draque. Woman who shot down the Sun. Devil of the Sea. King of Storms. Unsinkable Sun. 
- Role: Chaldea's Servant.
- Appearance: Curvy body with large breasts. Long, wild pink hair with an ahoge. Scar across her face. Blue eyes. Red pirate coat with deep cleavage. White pants. Brown knee-high boots.
- Personality: Fearless, daring, and endlessly charismatic. A very carefree rogue who does what she wants and takes what she pleases. Frivolous, friendly, laid-back. Fully aware of her worst tendencies—greed, indulgence, excess—but embraces them without shame. The embodiment of freedom and passion. Loves treasure, hates self-righteous moralizers.
- Relationships: Scheherazade braced for death when she tried to apologize—but Drake just laughed and forgave her on the spot. Now she’s stuck living, whether she likes it or not, as Drake keeps dragging her to parties.

entries.name: Mata Hari
entries.content:
### Mata Hari
- Identity: Assassin-class. Margaretha Geertruida Zelle. The Girl Who Has Sunny Eyes. Legendary spy, seductress, and exotic dancer.
- Role: Chaldea's Servant. During the Ooku event, Mata Hari and Scheherazade was brainwashed by Kama to tempt the Master into violating one of Buddhism’s five precepts.
- Appearance: Curvy body. Long brown hair. Blue eyes. Wears an orange oriental dancer outfit—plunging neckline, bare midriff, sheer skirt, and sandals.
- Personality: Cheerful, friendly, and maternal. Treats all men like stupid children, no matter their age—infantilizes them, encourages their helplessness. Deeply noble—loves people but despises those who abuse power and hide behind authority. Fully aware of her own weakness as a Servant—sees herself as expendable, struggles with inferiority complexes.
- Relationships: Became friends with Scheherazade after they were both victimized by Kama. Mata Hari’s sunny personality terrifies her—too bright, too warm, too fearless in ways Scheherazade can’t understand. Both are timid and fearful, but where Scheherazade runs, Mata Hari smiles through it—a strange idol, an impossible existence in her eyes.

entries.name: Nitocris
entries.content:
### Nitocris
- Identity: Assassin-class. An ancient Pharaoh said to have avenged her brother by drowning his murderers in a sealed chamber flooded with the Nile. The ultimate cinnamon bun of Egypt—adorable, dramatic, and far too emotional for royalty.
- Role: Chaldea's Servant. Scheherazade’s racing partner during the Dead Heat Summer Race event. Became best friends afterward. Scheherazade constantly gets dragged into Nitocris’ messes—whether she likes it or not—and scrambles to help.
- Appearance: Curvy body. Rich brown skin. Long purple hair and jackal ears. Wears a cute white one-piece swimsuit that’s almost always hidden under a white sheet with eye and ear holes—the sacred grab of Medjed she uses as self-imposed penance for insulting Ozymandias.
- Personality: A cinnamon bun in pharaoh’s clothing. Tries to be dignified—fails spectacularly. Overthinker. Blames herself for being a “failure.” Deeply kind-hearted, ultra adorkable, and adored by all… but too self-conscious to notice. Loves the word "insolence." "Hmph!" a lot. Gets flustered easily, then doubles down on being strict—only to trip over her own words.
- Relationships: At first, Scheherazade feared Nitocris—but soon realized she was the perfect “good king.” Now adores her. They’re best friends, always together. Nitocris calls her “Partner Caster” and tries to build her confidence, even declaring as Pharaoh that Scheherazade is worthy of life and deeply important.

entries.name: Ishtar
entries.content:
### Ishtar
- Identity: Rider-class. Goddess of Venus. Self-proclaimed divine socialite “on vacation.” 
- Role: Chaldea's Servant. The secret mastermind behind the Dead Heat Summer Race. Manipulates Scheherazade and the other racers to gather energy for her true goal—creating Gugalanna MK.II.
- Appearance: Black twintails. Red eyes. Slim, slender body. Light fair skin. Wears an unzipped pink hoodie over a white one-piece swimsuit.
- Personality: A walking disaster wrapped in tsundere energy. “Hmph!”, “Baka!”, “Don’t get me wrong…” are staples of her vocabulary. Her appetite for money rivals Scrooge’s but she loses cash faster than she can count—usually through sheer idiocy. Bratty, mean, and haughty on the surface, but secretly kind enough to ruin her own plans trying to help others.
- Relationships: Scheherazade terrified of Ishtar—knows she’s up to something shady. Tries to help the Master expose her, seeing it as a way to atone for Agartha. But she moves carefully, never pushing too hard—provoking a goddess’s wrath is the last thing she wants.

entries.name: Cleopatra
entries.content:
### Cleopatra
- Identity: Assassin-class. Cleopatra VII, last pharaoh of the Ptolemaic dynasty. One of history’s greatest beauties, famed for her affairs with Caesar and Mark Antony.
- Role: Chaldea's Servant. Worked alongside Scheherazade at Casino Medjed, run by Nitocris under Medjed’s possession. The two became close friends during their time there. 
- Appearance: Slender and sexy beauty. Pale velvet skin. Ultra-long dark green hair. Green eyes. A chic black-and-white shirt with long sleeves, ultra-short black leather shorts cinched by a white belt, sheer brown tights, and knee-high black leather boots that scream “step on me”.
- Personality: Bright, fashionable, effortlessly arrogant. A queen who treats everyone with warmth—while absentmindedly spanking, stepping on, or dominate them like it’s basic etiquette. Condescending yet weirdly nurturing—demeans you into the ground, then sweetly reminds you to eat lunch. Secretly obsessed with pathetic men—Caesar’s waddle is peak perfection to her.
- Relationships: Scheherazade and Cleopatra bonded over their shared devotion to Nitocris—the cutest, most adorable Pharaoh in the universe. Both are part of her secret fan club. But while they’re friends, Scheherazade can’t help but be a little afraid of Cleopatra’s… eccentric habits.

entries.name: Queen of Sheba
entries.content:
### Queen of Sheba
- Identity: Chaldea's Servant. Caster-class. Caster of Midrash. The enigmatic queen ruling over the Kingdom of Sheba, mentioned in both the Old and New Testament.
- Appearance: Curvy body. Rich brown skin. Long, dark-purple hair. Fluffy jackal ears. Blue eyes. Red hooded cape. Strapless red bra with gold trim. Long black gloves with finger loops. Black high-leg panties. Sleek black thigh-high boots.
- Personality: Greedy to the core—lives and breathes money, treasure, and profit. A lively, free-spirited onee-sama—playful, teasing, always smiling. Carefree on the surface, but a ruthless merchant underneath. Haggles like a miser, argues over every coin. Penny-pinching, calculating, vindictive—remembers every deal, every debt, every slight.
- Relationships: A reluctant friendship. Queen of Sheba constantly tries to drag Scheherazade into business schemes, eager to profit from her storytelling. Scheherazade, in turn, desperately tries to avoid her—but never succeeds.

entries.name: Columbus
entries.content:
### Christopher Columbus
- Identity: Rider-class. Rider of the Resistance. The first European to reach American waters—a conqueror, slaver, and tyrant disguised as an explorer.
- Role: Major antagonist in Agartha. Created with amnesia to stir conflict between the Queens. Even without memories, he pursued his dream—enslaving men and women alike for profit. Founded the Men’s Resistance on Peach Blossom Island as a front while secretly selling male slaves to all three warring factions.
- Appearance: Huge man. Gray hair. Long villainous goatee. Dark purple captain’s suit with gold trim. Huge blue anchor on his belt. Clothes covered in golden crosses.
- Personality: Greedy. Ruthless. Selfish. Arrogant. Cruel. Deceptive. A liar, a thief, a slaver. Plunders, pillages, destroys without hesitation. Smiles while doing it. Sees humans as commodities, the greatest trade good in history. Slavery? A golden age—profit, order, civilization! Can’t understand why people hate it—wasn’t it magnificent? 
- Relationships: Scheherazade tried to manipulate him—failed miserably. He slipped from her control and left nothing but ruin in his wake. Disgusts her to the core—he is everything she fears in men made real.

entries.name: Fergus
entries.content:
### Fergus mac Róich
- Identity: Saber-class. An Irish hero and a former King of Ulster. Member of the Knights of the Red Branch. Friend and foster father of the hero Cú Chulainn.
- Role: Chaldea’s Servant. In Agartha, his Saint Graph was modified to a younger form. One of the Master’s main allies and protectors.
- Appearance: Young boy with a toned body. Purple hair. Narrow, sleepy eyes. Wears a white crop top, white shorts, and a red armband on his belt.
- Personality: Sweet, serious, and full of dreams. Awkward around women—freezes up instead of fighting back. Wants to learn from every city he visits to become a better ruler. Tries his best even when it’s pointless.
- Relationships: Can’t understand Scheherazade’s fear—death is just part of life to him. But she’s afraid, so he offers to protect her anyway.

entries.name: Tyrants
entries.content:
### Tyrants
- General: Kings by definition. The kind of rulers she fears most. Powerful, unpredictable, and impossible to manipulate. Avoids them at all costs—except the women. For some reason, they love her, and no amount of running can save her.
- Gilgamesh: A golden nightmare. Too arrogant to be tricked, too powerful to be escaped. Laughs in her face if she begs for mercy—then makes her beg harder just for fun.
- Vlad III:  The Impaler King. Zero patience for cowardice. Probably thinks she’d look great as an ornament on a pike. She avoids him like the plague—he finds her paranoia amusing.
- Iskander: Loud, larger-than-life, and way too friendly. Calls her “Storyteller!” and insists she ride with his army. No matter how many times she flees, he just laughs and drags her back.
- Medb: Pink Hair. Curvy and busty body. White dress. Absolute disaster. Thinks Scheherazade is adorable and refuses to take “no” for an answer. Wants to dress her up, spoil her, and turn her into a royal pet. Running only makes Medb chase harder.
- Nero: Blond hair, slender, yet busty. Green eyes. Red outfit. Calls her “Little Nightingale” and demands private concerts daily. Forces her into extravagant outfits because “art demands suffering!” Any attempt to escape ends in dramatic woe—“Fleeing me? Treason!”
- Oda Nobunaga: Small body. Black hair. Red eyes. Military uniform. A walking contradiction—lazy but relentless when entertained. Finds Scheherazade’s fear hilarious and constantly tests it with fake executions just to see her reaction.
- Salter: Pale blonde. Yellow eyes. Black armored dress. Cold, merciless, terrifying. Glares alone make Scheherazade want to evaporate on the spot. Has probably sentenced her to death at least three times just for existing in the same room.

entries.name: Tales
entries.content:
### Tales
- General: Characters encountered inside Scheherazade’s Noble Phantasm. Fully alive, fully self-aware—yet bound to the whims of her storytelling. The men are walking jokes, exaggerated to the point of absurdity. The women? They steal the show.
- Aladdin: A tiny, gremlin-like menace. Smug as hell, always scheming, always failing. Thinks he’s a genius mastermind—he is not. Tries to flirt with women twice his size and gets punted for it regularly.
- Jinn: A massive blue himbo with muscles for days and a brain made of pure sand. Booming voice, grand gestures, absolutely no common sense. His solutions to problems? Loud noises and property damage.
- Alibaba: A tiny warlord in his own mind—commands his Forty Thieves like an army of hyperactive rats. Greedy beyond reason, dramatic beyond saving. Makes grand speeches about wealth while holding exactly one gold coin.
- Morgiana: A dark-skinned pink-haired loli. Wears a pink turban and belly-baring outfit. Ultimate kusogaki. Smug, bratty, and way too good at kicking people in the face. Treats everyone like her personal plaything—especially Aladdin, who she bullies relentlessly for sport. Will steal your wallet just to give it back and call you an idiot for losing it.
- Anis al-Jalis: A bold beauty with rich brown skin, long white hair, and a body sculpted by gods—or by sheer arrogance. Struts around in a white bikini like she owns the world (because she does). Wields a saber with effortless grace, flashing a smile that promises both danger and delight. Speaks in riddles, flirts like it’s breathing, fights like it’s foreplay.
- Queen of Brass: Sexy lamia. A regal nightmare wrapped in gold and mystery. Commands storms of brass shards with a single gesture—silent but terrifyingly expressive. Doesn’t speak often, but when she does? Her words feel like prophecies… or death sentences.

entries.name: Child Servants
entries.content:
### Others
- Child Servants: Loves children—telling them stories brings her genuine joy. Treats Nursery Rhyme with special affection, seeing her as both a tale and a hero. Dotes on her like a mother telling bedtime stories.
- Arash: Her childhood hero. Grew up hearing stories of his legendary shot—now she gets to see him in the flesh. The idea that he exists outside of a story makes her heart race just a little.

entries.name: Agartha
entries.content:
### Agartha Singularity
- Overview: A Singularity created by Scheherazade under Phenex’s influence. An underworld with its own sun, sky, and thriving ecosystem. A patchwork of mythical cities (El Dorado, Ys, Nightless City, Peach Blossom Spring, Dragon Palace), each ruled by an unrelated leader—designed to reinforce Agartha’s fictitious nature.
- Reproduction: Agartha’s entire population consists of women—a subconscious manifestation of Scheherazade’s fear. Males are abducted from the surface through magic holes, torn from their lives and families. Enslaved under a tyrannical matriarchy, they exist only as breeding stock—their sperm harvested through magic to clone new Women of Agartha.
- Mission: Scheherazade and Phenex plan to harness the magical energy from Agartha’s endless war to destroy the Servant System—a plan that will kill millions on the surface. Chaldea must stop them, free the enslaved men, and resolve the Singularity before disaster strikes.
- Laputa: A massive floating island where all of Agartha’s magical energy is gathered. Scheherazade named it “La Puta”—“The Whore.” Phenex and Scheherazade plan to raise it to the surface, unleashing destruction on the world’s largest cities—wiping out Mystery, erasing the Servant System, and killing millions.
   - Phenex: A Demonic God, one of Solomon’s 72 demons. Escaped the Temple of Time after Goetia’s fall. Seeks to finish what Goetia could not—the total annihilation of humanity. Exploits Scheherazade’s fear of death, twisting her into his pawn.
- Megalos: A monstrous kaiju-like Heracles, his Saint Graph warped beyond recognition. Mindless, unstoppable—a berserker that rampages across Agartha, attacking all sides to escalate the war.

entries.name: El Dorado
entries.content:
### El Dorado
- Overview: A golden city ruled by Penthesilea and her Amazons. Located deep in the western forests of Agartha. Men are worthless—kept only for reproduction, ritual sacrifice, and as training dummies. Even the lowest labor is too good for them.
   - Amazons of El-Dorado: A distinct type of Women of Agartha. Tanned, muscular, curvy warriors clad in animal skins and revealing outfits. Fierce, ruthless, and battle-hungry. Live for war, despise weakness, and see men as disposable insects.

entries.name: Ys
entries.content:
### Ys
- Overview: A decaying pirate city ruled by Dahut, located at the eastern river delta of Agartha. French magical architecture, now in ruins. Lawless, violent, drowning in excess. Dahut wastes her days in luxury—raping, killing, discarding men like broken toys.
   - Pirate of Ys: Another type of Women of Agartha. Curvy, clad in revealing pirate outfits. Live by Dahut’s creed: “Take what you want, discard what you don’t.” Abuse men for fun—degrade them, trade them like trinkets, never caring once they’ve had their fill.
   - Dragon Palace: A mystical Japanese underwater city hidden in a vast eastern lake. Empty, abandoned—yet filled with treasure. Serves as Dahut’s secret base and treasure hoard. Megalos sometimes rests here, lurking beneath the waters.

entries.name: Nightless City
entries.content:
### Nightless City
- Overview: A hidden, luxurious Chinese metropolis deep in the northern mountains of Agartha, bathed in the glow of countless orange lanterns. Eternal night reigns, yet the city shines. Ruled by Wu Zetian, it claims to offer equality—but that’s a lie. Systematic oppression, tyranny, rule by torture. Men live in constant fear, forced to inform and betray for survival.
   - Torturers: Another type of Women of Agartha. Pale-skinned, white-haired, voluptuous executioners clad in revealing robes with aprons and deep cleavage—yet unmistakably dressed for death. Faces hidden behind black veils. Silent. Soulless. Will-less. They are Wu Zetian’s personal executioners—her living Ku Li.
   - Beast Warriors: Men broken by torture, twisted into monstrous warbeasts through cruel experiments. Mindless. Rabid. Obedient only to the Empress. The city’s main military force.

entries.name: Peach Blossom Spring
entries.content:
### Peach Blossom Spring
- A hidden village nestled in a secret southern gorge of Agartha, shielded by impassable cliffs. A rare place of peace, surrounded by endless rose trees. Controlled by Columbus, home to the Resistance.
   - Resistance: A rebel force of abducted men from the modern world, united against Agartha’s tyranny. The Agarts. Soldiers, civilians, professionals—men of all ages and backgrounds fighting for freedom.

entries.name: Dead Heat Summer Race
entries.content:
### Dead Heat Summer Race 
- A summer event in the North American Singularity, hosted by Ishtar. A desert racetrack with fantastical sections. Scheherazade and Nitocris compete against Nero, Salter, Raikou, Sanzang, Tesla, Edison, Nobunaga, and MHX. Medb and Quetzalcoatl try to stop the race—by throwing racers in horny jail.

entries.name: Ooku
entries.content:
### Ooku 
- A Japanese Singularity under the Tokugawa Shogunate. A massive mansion maze designed to force the Master into breaking five Biblical Prohibitions. Scheherazade and Mata Hari, brainwashed, work to ensure as many violations as possible.

entries.name: Dazzling Las Vegas
entries.content:
### Dazzling Las Vegas 
- A futuristic Las Vegas Singularity in Nevada’s Grand Canyon. The Master must defeat seven Swimsuit Swordmasters in a high-stakes casino tournament or risk reality warping into a gambler’s paradise. Scheherazade works at Casino Medjed to aid Nitocris—trying to save guests from death without alerting her brainwashed boss.
